Platform.Database.Connector.Dbf.Title: DBF/CDX/FPT Native Storage
Platform.Database.Connector.Dbf.Translat: Copperfin should treat legacy xBase storage as a first-class runtime and design-time store.
Platform.Database.Connector.JsonApi.Tran: JSON-backed services need schema discovery and dynamic projection to feel browseable through xBase-style commands.
Platform.Database.Connector.Mongodb.Tran: Document stores need projection and predicate translation from FoxPro-style queries into dynamic document pipelines.
Platform.Database.Connector.Oracle.Title: Oracle
Platform.Database.Connector.Oracle.Trans: Oracle stays in the first-class relational path even when syntax normalization is required.
Platform.Database.Connector.Postgresql.T: FoxPro-style SQL can map to PostgreSQL with a deterministic relational translator and optional extensions such as pgvector.
Platform.Database.Connector.Sqlite.Title: SQLite
Platform.Database.Connector.Sqlite.Trans: FoxPro-style SQL can be translated through a deterministic SQL dialect mapper for straightforward relational workloads.
Platform.Database.Connector.SqlServer.Tr: FoxPro-style SQL can map to SQL Server through a deterministic relational translator with stored procedure and security-policy support.
Platform.Database.Connector.Vector.Title: Vector/Embedding Stores
Platform.Database.Connector.Vector.Trans: Vector stores need semantic-search operators, embedding pipelines, and optional AI-assisted query planning around deterministic connector rules.
Platform.Database.Guardrail.AiPlanningOp: AI-assisted query planning stays optional, policy-controlled, and outside the trusted execution core.
Platform.Database.Guardrail.BrowseableSc: Document and vector backends should expose browseable schema hints even when the source is dynamic or sparse.
Platform.Database.Guardrail.Deterministi: Deterministic translators come first for relational backends and other straightforward mappings.
Platform.Database.Guardrail.ExplainableC: Connector failures must be explainable so developers know when Copperfin translated a query directly and when it needed a planner.
Platform.Database.QueryPath.FoxSqlDocume: Lower simple selects and filters deterministically, then allow optional AI assistance for ambiguous nested-document reshaping.
Fox SQL To Document Query Plan
Platform.Database.QueryPath.FoxSqlRelati: Build a canonical Copperfin query AST and lower it deterministically into each relational backend dialect.
Platform.Database.QueryPath.FoxSqlVector: Use deterministic retrieval templates first, then optionally ask an approved AI model to help synthesize semantic ranking or hybrid-search plans.
Fox SQL To Vector Retrieval Plan
Platform.Database.QueryPath.XbaseBrowseD: Translate browse/filter intent into field projection, path navigation, and document predicates.
Platform.Database.QueryPath.XbasePolyglo: Normalize xBase intent into Copperfin commands that each connector can execute or reject with an explainable compatibility result.
Platform.Extensibility.AiFeature.AiAssis: Optional vibe-coding and code-intelligence helpers for designers, migration, and diagnostics.
Platform.Extensibility.AiFeature.AiDebug: Allow developers to send debugger context, stack traces, and runtime telemetry to an approved assistant workflow for optional debugging help.
Platform.Extensibility.AiFeature.LocalMo: Use local or enterprise-approved models rather than forcing one hosted provider.
Platform.Extensibility.AiFeature.McpHost: Expose Copperfin tools through an MCP host so developers can use preferred AI models and assistants.
Platform.Extensibility.AiFeature.ModelSe: Let developers choose the model used for AI debugging and assistance instead of hard-coding one provider or model family.
Platform.Extensibility.DotNetOutput.Prim: Copperfin applications should be able to ship as native executables with first-class .NET compatibility, and selected modules should be exposable as managed wrappers or NuGet-consumable SDK outputs.
Platform.Extensibility.DotNetInteropDeci: allowed by policy with audit-required path
estimated latency exceeds in-process policy budget
reflection on untrusted input is blocked
Platform.Extensibility.DotNetParity.Inse: Rejected due to known unsafe behavior and exploit history.
Platform.Extensibility.DotNetParity.Json: Provide high-value JSON conversion features while preserving native null/blank semantics.
Platform.Extensibility.DotNetParity.Lega: Rejected because emulating retired CAS behavior adds complexity with little user value.
Platform.Extensibility.DotNetParity.Task: Expose async/await-style behavior through FP/VFP-friendly command and function facades.
Platform.Extensibility.DotNetParity.Unsa: Rejected due to trust-boundary and policy-audit risks.
Platform.Extensibility.Guardrail.AiTooli: MCP and AI tooling are opt-in developer features with audit, provider policy, and user-selected model controls.
Platform.Extensibility.Guardrail.DotNetP: .NET interop is first-class, but managed loading is policy-controlled and auditable.
Platform.Extensibility.Guardrail.NativeF: The trusted execution core stays native-first and security-first.
Platform.Extensibility.Guardrail.Release: Release outputs must preserve a clear .NET consumption story even when the executable is native.
Platform.Extensibility.Guardrail.Sidecar: Python and R are supported through sidecars or job runners, not as the product core.
Platform.Extensibility.Language.CAbi.Out: Performance-sensitive extensions can be linked or loaded through stable native interfaces.
Platform.Extensibility.Language.DotNet.O: Managed assemblies can be called from Copperfin and Copperfin logic can be surfaced as .NET-consumable outputs.
Platform.Extensibility.Language.Python.O: Python support is positioned as a sidecar or job facility for data science and automation, not the trusted core.
Platform.Extensibility.Language.R.Output: R support is positioned as a sidecar or job facility for statistical computing, reporting, and reproducible data-science workflows.
Platform.Extensibility.Language.R.Title: R Analytics And Statistical Jobs
Platform.Extensibility.Language.Rust.Out: Rust is acceptable for safety-sensitive helpers behind stable native interfaces.
Platform.Extensibility.Language.Xbase.Ou: Primary runtime and build target for FoxPro-style applications.
